subject.title: feat: allow standalone MCP Apps to use bound tools and resources

question: Should a short-lived standalone MCP App ticket be authorized to invoke the owning server’s app-visible tools and read its resources under the proposed view-bound checks?
rationale: This is an intentional expansion of browser authority rather than a mechanical bug repair; code review can assess containment, but maintainers must choose whether the product’s ticket threat model permits this capability.

options.title: Approve the bounded bridge
options.body: Accept the least-privilege capability after final-head security and gateway checks confirm that only the live owning-server view can use it.

options.title: Keep standalone views read-only
options.body: Reject tool and resource authority for ticketed hosts and retain the existing rendering-only standalone model.

options.title: Narrow the allowed operations
options.body: Permit only a smaller resource or tool subset if the broader bridge exceeds the desired ticket authority.

recommendation.title: Approve the bounded bridge
recommendation.body: Accept the least-privilege capability after final-head security and gateway checks confirm that only the live owning-server view can use it.

likelyOwner.reason: They recently merged adjacent MCP App authority work and authored the shared bridge design.
